name: Kiron Labs - Content Curation Engine v1

parameters.content:
## Content Curation Engine v1 (v2 — client-agnostic)

Shared heavy logic, invoked by any client's Caller workflow via **Execute Workflow**. This Engine holds NO per-client identity (no Telegram bot, no social credentials) — n8n binds credentials per node at design time, not per run, so a bot/social credential can't be swapped dynamically inside a shared node. Sending to Telegram (and, later, publishing to social) is each client's own responsibility, done in their own Caller, with their own bot.

What IS safely shared here: RSS fetch, dedup, DeepSeek relevance filter + draft generation, and Sheets read/write — `spreadsheet_id`/`sources_tab`/`content_tab` are parameters, so each client can own their own spreadsheet file (shared with the automation's Google account) without forking this workflow.

**Output contract:** this workflow always ends at one of four leaf `Set` nodes, and whichever one actually ran is what `Execute Workflow` returns to the Caller: `{outcome: 'limit_reached' | 'no_new_content' | 'dry_run' | 'pending_review', ...}`. The Caller decides what to do with each outcome, including whether/how to notify Telegram.

**Credentials needed:**
- `Google Sheets - Rob` (OAuth2) — reused as-is; this is the automation's Google account, granted access to whichever client spreadsheet it's pointed at. Works for any client's own file, no new credential needed per client.
- `DeepSeek API - Rob` (Generic Credential / HTTP Header Auth, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`) — reused as-is. DeepSeek isn't a per-client identity the way a bot is, so one shared key is fine; split it later only if billing needs to be separated per client, which just means swapping this one credential reference, not restructuring the workflow.
- `Telegram - Rob` — used ONLY by the Error Trigger branch at the bottom, which is Rob's own ops/monitoring channel (platform operator, not a client-facing bot) — intentionally the one hardcoded exception, since a broken Engine affects every client and needs one place to report to.

**Input contract (from Execute Workflow Trigger):**
```
{ profile, channel, spreadsheet_id, sources_tab, content_tab,
  daily_limit, system_prompt_relevance, system_prompt_draft, dry_run }
```

nodes.name: Engine Input
nodes.notes: No telegram_chat_id here on purpose — the Engine never talks to Telegram. See Sticky Note.

nodes.name: Analyze Content Log
nodes.notes: Uses $now (Luxon, respects the workflow/instance timezone) instead of new Date().toISOString(), which is UTC and can misclassify 'today' near midnight in America/Mexico_City (UTC-6). No 'profile' filter on rows anymore — BarMon-Content has no profile column (removed 2026-08-20, redundant since each client now has their own spreadsheet), so every row in this tab already belongs to this run's profile by construction. Only 'channel' still distinguishes rows within the tab.

nodes.name: Build Result - Limit Reached
nodes.notes: Leaf node — no Telegram send here. The Caller reads outcome='limit_reached' from Execute Workflow's return and decides whether/how to notify.

nodes.name: Filter Active Sources
nodes.notes: Only rows with active = TRUE are used.

nodes.name: Read RSS Feed
nodes.notes: Runs once per active source. If a feed is broken this item errors and the whole execution fails fast (fires the Error Trigger) — fix or deactivate the source row rather than silently skipping it.

nodes.name: Tag Source Name
nodes.notes: Re-derives source_name via $runIndex since RSS Feed Read loses it (each run corresponds to one input source item, in order).

nodes.name: Build Result - No New Content
nodes.notes: Leaf node — no Telegram send here.

nodes.name: DeepSeek - Filter Relevance
nodes.notes: Fixed auth: DeepSeek has no native n8n credential type. Uses a Generic Credential (HTTP Header Auth) the same way the production Rob-LinkedIn workflow does. Expects strict JSON: {"selected_index": N, "day_topic": "...", "reason": "..."}. Fails fast on malformed output (fires the Error Trigger) rather than silently picking a wrong article.

nodes.name: DeepSeek - Generate Draft
nodes.notes: Channel-specific draft — system_prompt_draft comes from the Caller, so the same Engine call produces different tone/length/CTA depending on which Caller invoked it.

nodes.name: Build Content Row
nodes.notes: Computes content_hash (SHA-256, full length — truncation for Telegram callback_data happens in the Caller, not here) and a safety-net dedup check against recent_hashes. 'profile' stays in this payload for the Caller's own messages/logging, but is NOT written to BarMon-Content — the next node maps columns explicitly and simply doesn't include it, since the sheet has no profile column.

nodes.name: Build Result - Dry Run
nodes.notes: Matches the production Rob-LinkedIn convention: dry run does NOT write to Sheets, it only returns the draft so the Caller can preview it via Telegram (its own bot).

nodes.name: Log Draft (Pending Review)
nodes.notes: Explicit column mapping (not autoMapInputData) so extra fields carried in the input JSON for downstream use (profile, dry_run, spreadsheet_id, content_tab) are never written as stray columns — only the 11 real BarMon-Content columns are mapped. No 'profile' column (removed 2026-08-20).

nodes.name: Build Result - Pending Review
nodes.notes: Leaf node. The Caller uses content_hash to build the Telegram Approve/Discard buttons (truncated to 16 chars there, per Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit) and to update telegram_message_id afterward.

nodes.name: Error Trigger
nodes.notes: Fires on ANY failed node in this workflow. Fail-fast by design. This is the one deliberate exception to 'no client identity inside the Engine' — it's Rob's own ops channel, not a client-facing bot, and a broken Engine affects every client at once, so one shared alert destination makes sense here.
